Tone facts stated in passing: grammatical tone contrast on pronominal clitics, "In TSK, the regular (indicative) 2Pl ó morpheme has high tone, contrasting with 2P

sources.citation: CSLI Publications catalogue page for Heath 2005 (publisher's blurb).
sources.note: Nothing on stress. TSK's tone system, quite different from more familiar Bantu tone systems'.

sources.citation: Nicolaï, Robert. 1981. Les dialectes du songhay: contribution à l'étude des changements linguistiques. Paris: SELAF.
sources.access_detail: open copy posted by the author (located 2026-09-25); a digital copy (available on request)
sources.locator: Carte A 'Le pays songhay: points d'enquete' and Carte 21 legend p. 278 (PDF 287): survey points list Hombori, Tinie, Marense for 'songhay central'; no Kikara /…
sources.note: This work describes Songhay dialects surveyed by Nicolai: songhay occidental (Djenne, Tombouctou = Koyra Chiini), songhay oriental (Bamba, Gao, Alkaseybaten, Gabero = Koyraboro Senni), songhay central (Hombori, Tinie, Marense = Humburi Senni), kaado (Dolbel, S. The work does not describe this language. Nearest variety covered is 'songhay central' = Hombori (humb1243), graded below. Heath's §1.6 'Prior Literature' (p. 8) implies earlier notice of the Kikara-area variety; Nicolaï's dialect survey is the likely source and includes tonal/accentual notes on Songhay dialects.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2010. Change Request Number 2010-006: adopted create [tst] (2011-05-18). Dallas: SIL International.https://iso639-3.sil.org/request/2010-006(change-request file; accompanying form: Hochstetler, Lee (requester), 'Request for New Language Code Element in ISO 639-3: Tondi Songway Kiini', dated 2009-12-17, 4 pp.).
sources.note: A code-request form, not a description; its only linguistic characterisation (section 3c, p.2) quotes the publisher's blurb of Heath 2005: TSK 'is a tonal language' that, unlike other Songhay languages, 'preserves the lexical and grammatical tones of its proto-language'. Third-hand; no inventory or analysis.

tone.quote: Not sure which Songhay language is closest linguistically. From Amazon.com: "Tondi Songway Kiini (TSK) is a tonal language…. Unlike other Songhay languages, TSK preserves the lexical and grammatical tones of its proto-language and also exhibits unique systems for the expression of focalization and relativization."
